Psalms 12:1: For the end. A psalm of David.
Psalms 12:2: How long, Lord, wilt Thou forget me utterly? How long wilt Thou turn Thy face away from me?
Psalms 12:3: How long shall I place counsels within my soul, pains within my heart by day? How long will my enemy be raised above me?
Psalms 12:4: Look; hear me, Lord my God. Give light to my eyes, lest I fall asleep into death,
Psalms 12:5: lest my enemy say, “I prevailed against him.” Those who afflict me will exult if I am shaken.
Psalms 12:6: But I have hoped in Thy mercy; my heart will exult in Thy salvation. I will sing to the Lord, who has benefited me, and I will sing praise to the name of the Lord Most High.
Job 19:6: Know, then, that the Lord is the One who disturbed me and raised His stronghold against me.
Job 19:7: Behold, I laugh in reproach and will not speak; I will cry out, but judgment is nowhere.
Job 19:8: I have been walled in all around and cannot pass through; He placed darkness before my face.
Isaiah 59:12: For our lawlessness is great before Thee, and our sins have opposed us. Our lawless deeds are within us, and we have recognized our wrongs:
Isaiah 59:13: We acted impiously and lied and withdrew from following our God. We spoke unjust things and disobeyed; we conceived and meditated on unjust words from our heart.
Isaiah 59:14: We drove judgment backward, and righteousness has withdrawn far away, for truth was consumed in their ways, and they could not go straight through.
Isaiah 59:15: Truth has been taken away, and they turned their mind away from understanding. The Lord saw, and it did not please Him that there was no judgment.
Acts 13:38: Therefore let it be known to you, men, brothers, that through Him forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you; and from everything from which you could not be justified in the law of Moses,
Acts 13:39: in Him everyone who believes is justified.
Acts 13:40: Take care, then, lest what is spoken in the prophets come upon you:
Acts 13:41: ‘Look, you scoffers, marvel and vanish, for I am doing a work in your days, a work you will never believe even if someone recounts it to you.’”
Jeremiah 5:15: Behold, I am bringing a nation upon you from far away, house of Israel, says the Lord, a nation whose language’s sound you will not understand.
Jeremiah 5:17: and they will devour your harvest and your bread, and devour your sons and daughters, and devour your sheep and calves, and devour your vineyards and fig orchards and olive groves; and with a sword they will thresh your fortified cities, in which you have trusted.
Isaiah 10:5: Woe to the Assyrians! The rod of My anger and wrath is in their hands.
Isaiah 10:6: I will send My anger against a lawless nation, and I will command My people to take spoils and plunder, trample the cities and reduce them to dust.
Isaiah 10:7: But he did not consider it this way and has not reckoned it this way in his soul; rather, his mind will turn aside, even to destroy not a few nations.
Isaiah 10:8: If they say to him, “You alone are ruler,”
Isaiah 10:9: he will say, “Did I not take the country above Babylon and Chalanneh, where the tower was built? I also took Arabia, Damascus and Samaria.
Isaiah 10:10: As I took these in my hand, I will also take all the dominions. Wail, carved images in Jerusalem and Samaria!
Isaiah 10:11: For as I did to Samaria and her handmade objects, so I will also do to Jerusalem and her idols.”
Isaiah 10:12: When the Lord has finished doing all things on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, He will bring judgment upon the great mind—the ruler of the Assyrians—and upon the height of the glory of his eyes.
Isaiah 10:13: For he said, “By strength I will act, and by the wisdom of understanding. I will remove nations’ boundaries, plunder their strength and shake inhabited cities.
Isaiah 10:14: I will seize the whole inhabited world in my hand like a nest, and lift it like abandoned eggs. There is no one who will escape me or contradict me.”
Deuteronomy 28:49: The Lord shall bring against you a nation from afar, from the end of the earth, as the swooping of an eagle, a nation whose speech you shall not understand,
Deuteronomy 28:50: a nation shameless of countenance, which shall not regard the face of the aged, nor have mercy upon the young.
Deuteronomy 28:51: And it shall consume the offspring of your cattle and the produce of your land, leaving you neither grain, nor wine, nor oil, nor the herds of your cattle, nor the flocks of your sheep, until it destroys you.
Deuteronomy 28:52: And it shall wear you down in all your cities, until your high and fortified walls wherein you trust are cast down throughout all your land; and it shall afflict you in all your cities which the Lord your God has given you.
2 Kings 24:10: At that time Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.
2 Kings 24:11: Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon entered the city while his servants were besieging it.
2 Kings 24:12: Joakim king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he, his servants, his mother, his rulers, and his eunuchs. The king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.
2 Kings 24:13: He brought out from there all the treasures of the Lord’s house and the treasures of the king’s house. He cut apart all the gold vessels Solomon king of Israel had made in the Lord’s sanctuary, according to the Lord’s word.
2 Kings 24:14: He deported Jerusalem, all the rulers, and the mighty in strength, taking ten thousand captives, and every craftsman and one who shuts up. None remained except the land’s poor.
2 Kings 24:15: He deported Joakim to Babylon, along with the king’s mother, the king’s wives, and his eunuchs. He led the land’s powerful men into deportation from Jerusalem to Babylon,
2 Kings 24:16: and all the men of the force, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and those who shut up, one thousand—all mighty men who waged war. The king of Babylon brought them into deportation to Babylon.
Ezekiel 26:7: For thus says the Lord: I am bringing against you, Tyre, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the north—he is king of kings—with horses, chariots, horsemen, and an assembly of very many nations.
Ezekiel 26:8: He will kill your daughters in the plain with the sword, set an advance guard against you, build around you, and make a palisade and a ring of weapons around you; he will set his spears opposite you.
Ezekiel 26:9: He will throw down your walls and your towers with his swords.
Psalms 72:1: A psalm of Asaph. How good God is to Israel, to those upright in heart!
Psalms 72:2: But my feet were almost shaken; my steps were nearly poured out.
Psalms 72:3: For I envied the lawless, beholding sinners’ peace,
Psalms 72:4: for there is no refusal at their death, and firmness in their scourging.
Psalms 72:5: They are not in human toils, and they will not be scourged with humans.
Psalms 72:6: Therefore arrogance seized them; they wrapped themselves in their injustice and ungodliness.
Psalms 72:7: Their injustice will come out as though from fat; they passed into a disposition of heart.
Psalms 72:8: They devised and spoke in wickedness; they spoke injustice against the height.
Psalms 72:9: They set their mouth toward heaven, and their tongue passed over the earth.
Psalms 72:10: Therefore my people will return here, and full days will be found for them.
Psalms 72:11: And they said, “How did God know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?”
Psalms 72:12: Behold, these are sinners, and they prosper; for the age they took possession of wealth.
Psalms 72:13: And I said, “Then in vain I made my heart righteous and washed my hands among the innocent;
Psalms 72:14: and I became scourged all day, and my rebuke comes in the mornings.”
Ecclesiastes 9:11: Again I saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor battle to the mighty, nor bread to the wise, nor wealth to those with understanding, nor favor to those with knowledge; for time and encounter will happen to them all.
Ecclesiastes 9:12: For a person does not know his time: like fish caught in an evil net, and birds caught in a snare, so human beings are trapped at an evil time when it falls upon them suddenly.
